definition_zh: 电的；与电有关的；电气的；用电的
definition_en: relating to electricity as a system, to electrical engineering, or to equipment that runs on electricity
core_image: 配电箱盖一打开，一排排彩色线束和标签露出来
scene: 电工掀开墙上的盖板，露出一排烧焦的线头。An electrical fault had started the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 electrical 是「与电有关的、电气的」（第 1 个义项：指电力系统与线路，而非单个电器）；句意是线路中一处电气故障引发了火灾。

pos.zh: 形容词：电的；与电有关的；电气的；用电的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -al 得到，义为「电的；用电的」
由 electric 加 -ity 构成，义为「电；电力」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「用电力地；在电气方面」

senses.title: Relating to electrical systems
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a system of supply, wiring and engineering
senses.definitionCN: 指作为供电、布线与工程系统的电
senses.example: She studied electrical engineering at college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学的是电气工程。
senses.why: The -al ending turns the noun electricity into a word about the field as a whole, so it suits systems rather than single devices.
senses.whyCN: -al 词尾把名词 electricity 变成指整个领域的词，因此它适合系统而不适合单个器具。

senses.title: Running on electricity
senses.definition: of equipment or appliances, operated by electricity, used as a general classifying word
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或器具由电力驱动，用作一般分类的说法
senses.example: Old electrical appliances use far more power.
senses.exampleCN: 旧家用电器耗电多得多。
senses.why: A whole class of goods is sorted by what drives them, so the classifying adjective takes the -al form.
senses.whyCN: 一整类商品按驱动方式分类，于是这个分类形容词采用了 -al 形式。

senses.title: Of the theory of electricity
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of electricity and its properties
senses.definitionCN: 指对电及其性质的科学理论研究
senses.example: The paper compares the electrical properties of the two metals.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文比较了两种金属的电学性质。
senses.why: Properties belong to the science rather than to a machine, so the academic sense also takes -al.
senses.whyCN: 性质属于科学而不属于某台机器，所以学术义也用 -al 形式。

intro.en: Electrical is electric plus the Latin adjective ending -al; the stem goes back through Latin electrum to Greek elektron, amber.
intro.cn: electrical 是 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al；词干经拉丁语 electrum 上溯到希腊语 elektron（琥珀）。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the substance that first showed the effect.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，是最先显现这种效应的物质。

items.en: Seventeenth-century science coined electricus for the force amber shows.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学造出 electricus，指琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English took the adjective and used it for bodies that attract and repel.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用于相互吸引与排斥的物体。

items.en: The -al form was added to speak of the whole field rather than one object.
items.cn: 加上 -al 的形式用来谈整个领域，而不是单个物体。

items.en: Engineering, wiring and appliances settled into the -al branch, leaving electric for the vivid and the specific.
items.cn: 工程、布线与家电固定在 -al 这一支，把 electric 留给更具体、更生动的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates electric, electronic and powered.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组区分 electric、electronic 与 powered。

entries.definition: Of electricity itself, or of one device that runs on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」，多指力量本身或单个器具。

entries.definition: The energy of moving charges, or its supply to homes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电；电力」。

entries.definition: By means of electricity, or in electrical terms.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「用电力地；在电气方面」。

entries.definition: A tradesperson who fits and repairs wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: Working through circuits that control electrons, as phones and computers do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电子的电路工作，如手机与电脑。

entries.definition: Driven by a named source, such as solar-powered.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「以……为动力的」，须说明来源。

entries.definition: The public supply of electricity to a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「市电、供电网」，是 electrical 系统的来源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks open a fuse box, then draw the line between a single device and the whole system behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子打开一个配电箱，再划清「单个器具」与「背后整套系统」的界线。

normal.en: The -al makes it about the field: electrical engineering, electrical fault.
normal.cn: -al 让它指向整个领域：电气工程、电气故障。

normal.en: An electric kettle is one object; electrical wiring is the system feeding it.
normal.cn: electric kettle 是一件东西；electrical wiring 是给它供电的系统。

normal.en: Electrical appliances as a class, not one appliance in the hand.
normal.cn: electrical appliances 指一整类，而不是手里那一件。

normal.en: Electrical properties belong to the science, not to the plug.
normal.cn: electrical properties 属于科学，而不属于插头。

normal.en: Electric can thrill; electrical stays technical.
normal.cn: electric 可以令人激动；electrical 始终偏技术。

abstract.en: Picture the inside of a fuse box, rows of coloured wires and labels.
abstract.cn: 想象配电箱内部，一排排彩色导线与标签。

abstract.en: The same current that lights a lamp also has a name as a system.
abstract.cn: 点亮灯泡的那股电流，作为系统另有一个名称。

abstract.en: Electrical is the map; electric is the spark on it.
abstract.cn: electrical 是地图；electric 是地图上那颗火花。

examples.en: She studied electrical engineering at college.
examples.cn: 她在大学学的是电气工程。

examples.en: Old electrical appliances use far more power.
examples.cn: 旧家用电器耗电多得多。

examples.en: The paper compares the electrical properties of the two metals.
examples.cn: 这篇论文比较了两种金属的电学性质。

root: 由 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al 构成；electric 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 与近代拉丁语 electricus 而来。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electrical: the supply system, equipment classified by its power source, and the science of electricity.
sensesIntro.cn: electrical 的三个义项：供电与线路系统、按动力分类的电器，以及电学理论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open fuse box with rows of coloured wires and labels.
core.cn: 核心意象：打开的配电箱，成排彩色导线与标签。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: supply, wiring and the engineering that runs them.
branches.cn: 系统线：供电、布线以及管理它们的工程。

branches.en: THE CLASS: appliances sorted by what drives them.
branches.cn: 分类线：按驱动方式归类的一整批电器。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: properties studied rather than used.
branches.cn: 科学线：被研究而非被使用的性质。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the system and the goods it feeds form one grid.
branches.cn: 供给线：系统与它供养的电器构成一张电网。

branches.en: THE THEORY: every fault is a lesson in the science.
branches.cn: 理论线：每一次故障都是科学的一课。

intro.en: Electrical is electric plus the Latin adjective -al; the whole branch stays close to the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electrical 是 electric 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -al；整支词都与希腊语「琥珀」保持很近的距离。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus and the -al form are later scientific constructions.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 有记录；electricus 与加 -al 的形式则是后来的科学构造。

definition_zh: 电；电能；电力供应；电学；（紧张兴奋的）气氛
definition_en: the energy carried by moving electric charges, the supply of such energy to buildings, the science that studies it, or a feeling of tense excitement in a crowd
core_image: 灯泡里的细丝骤然发亮，电流沿铜线一路奔涌
scene: 暴雨整夜拍打窗户，村里一片漆黑，只有诊所的发电机还在响。The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 electricity 是「电力供应」（第 2 个义项：输送到住宅与村镇的电）；句意是这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。

pos.zh: 名词：电；电能；电力供应；电学；紧张兴奋的气氛

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ity 得到，义为「电的；用电的」
由 electric 加 -al 构成，义为「电气的；与电有关的」
由 electric 加 -ian 构成，义为「电工」
由 electric 加动词后缀 -fy 构成，义为「使通电；使震惊」

senses.title: The energy of moving charges
senses.definition: the energy produced by the movement of electric charges, which can light a lamp or drive a machine
senses.definitionCN: 由电荷运动产生的能量，可以点灯或驱动机器
senses.example: Copper wire carries electricity well.
senses.exampleCN: 铜线导电性能很好。
senses.why: The -ity ending turns the adjective electric into a noun of quality, and that quality is the energy a charged body holds.
senses.whyCN: -ity 词尾把形容词 electric 变成表性质的名词，而带电物体所持有的那种性质就是这股能量。

senses.title: A supply to buildings
senses.definition: the supply of electric power through wires to homes, offices and streets
senses.definitionCN: 通过电线输送到住宅、办公室与街道的电力
senses.example: The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。
senses.why: Once the energy is piped into buildings, the abstract force becomes a service that can be billed or cut off.
senses.whyCN: 这股能量一旦被送进建筑，抽象的力量就变成一项能开账单、也能被切断的服务。

senses.title: The science of the force
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies electric charge, current and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 研究电荷、电流及其效应的物理学分支
senses.example: He is reading a history of electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 他正在读一部电学史。
senses.why: A named force needs a science, and English let the same noun do both jobs instead of coining a separate term.
senses.whyCN: 一股被命名的力需要一门科学，而英语让同一个名词兼做两件事，没有另造新词。

senses.title: A charged atmosphere
senses.definition: a feeling of tense excitement that seems to fill a room or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛充满整个房间或人群的紧张兴奋感
senses.example: There was electricity in the air before the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会开始前，空气里满是紧张兴奋的气氛。
senses.why: A charged body makes hair stand up, and a charged room makes people tense, so the physical charge lends its name to excitement.
senses.whyCN: 带电的物体会让汗毛竖起，带电的房间会让人紧绷，于是物理的电荷把名字借给了兴奋感。

intro.en: Electricity is electric plus the Latin noun ending -ity; electric itself goes back through Latin electrum to Greek elektron, amber, whose rubbed surface first showed attraction.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity；electric 本身经拉丁语 electrum 上溯到希腊语 elektron（琥珀），琥珀摩擦后的表面最先显现出吸引现象。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the resin that crackles and attracts when rubbed.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，这种树脂摩擦后会噼啪作响并吸引碎屑。

items.en: Latin took the word as electrum, naming both amber and a pale gold-silver alloy.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 electrum，既指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的金银合金。

items.en: Seventeenth-century experimenters coined electricus for bodies that attract and repel after rubbing.
items.cn: 十七世纪的实验者造出 electricus，指摩擦后能吸引与排斥的物体。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and used it for the force as well as the objects.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，既用于物体，也用于那股力。

items.en: Adding -ity produced a noun for the force itself, recorded in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 加上 -ity 造出指这股力本身的名词，十七世纪已有记载。

items.en: The utility sense and the metaphor of a charged room grew out of the same noun.
items.cn: 供电义与「带电房间」的比喻，都是从同一个名词里长出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates the energy from power, current and energy itself.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组把这份「电」与 power、current、energy 区分开。

entries.definition: Of the force itself, or of one device that runs on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」，多指力量本身或单个器具。

entries.definition: Of electricity as a system of wiring and engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，指布线与工程意义上的电。

entries.definition: A tradesperson who installs and repairs wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电工」。

entries.definition: To charge with electricity, or to thrill someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使通电；使震惊」。

entries.definition: The supply of energy to a building, often used for electricity in the home.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电力、动力」，常用来指住宅的供电。

entries.definition: The flow of charge through a wire; a rate, not the energy itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电流」，指电荷在导线中的流动，是速率而非能量本身。

entries.definition: The general capacity to do work, of which electricity is one form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能量」，是做功的一般能力，电只是其中一种形式。

entries.definition: The plain word for the feeling that the charged metaphor describes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「兴奋」，是那种带电气氛所比喻的直白说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from amber rubbed in the dark and follow the spark into wires, bills and a tense room.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从黑暗中摩擦的琥珀出发，让火花一路走进电线、电费单与紧绷的房间。

normal.en: Electric plus -ity: the quality of being electric becomes a substance you can bill.
normal.cn: electric 加 -ity：带电的性质变成一种能开账单的东西。

normal.en: Amber rubbed on wool is the first experiment behind the word.
normal.cn: 琥珀在羊毛上摩擦，是这个词背后最早的那个实验。

normal.en: Static electricity clings; current electricity flows.
normal.cn: static electricity 停在原地；current electricity 沿导线流动。

normal.en: Cut off the electricity and the whole village goes dark.
normal.cn: 切断 electricity，整个村子就黑了。

normal.en: A room full of electricity is a room where nobody can sit still.
normal.cn: 满是 electricity 的房间，就是没人坐得住的那个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a copper wire as a river, with charge instead of water.
abstract.cn: 把铜线想成一条河，河里流的不是水，而是电荷。

abstract.en: The same river can be a science, a bill, or a mood.
abstract.cn: 同一条河可以是一门科学、一张账单，也可以是一种情绪。

abstract.en: Electricity is a name for a force that behaves like a fluid and a feeling.
abstract.cn: electricity 是一股力的名字，它既像流体，又像情绪。

examples.en: Copper wire carries electricity well.
examples.cn: 铜线导电性能很好。

examples.en: The storm cut off the electricity to the whole village.
examples.cn: 这场暴风雨切断了整个村子的供电。

examples.en: There was electricity in the air before the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会开始前，空气里满是紧张兴奋的气氛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一来克锤西提」——按下开关，铜线里那股劲儿立刻冲到灯泡里

root: 由 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity 构成；electric 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 与近代拉丁语 electricus 而来。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of electricity: the energy itself, the supply to buildings, the science that studies it, and the metaphor of a tense room.
sensesIntro.cn: electricity 的四个义项：能量本身、输送到建筑的供电、研究它的学科，以及「紧绷房间」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filament flaring inside a bulb as current races along a copper wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：电流沿铜线奔涌，灯泡里的细丝骤然发亮。

branches.en: THE ENERGY: charge in motion, measured and used.
branches.cn: 能量线：运动中的电荷，被计量、被使用。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the same energy delivered as a service.
branches.cn: 供给线：同一股能量以服务的形式送到门口。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the force turned into an object of study.
branches.cn: 学科线：这股力变成被研究的对象。

branches.en: THE FEELING: a charged room borrows the physical word.
branches.cn: 情绪线：带电的房间借用了这个物理词。

branches.en: THE CURRENT: what flows in the wire is what arrives at the socket.
branches.cn: 电流线：导线里流动的东西，正是插座里到达的东西。

intro.en: Electricity is electric plus the Latin noun ending -ity; the stem behind it is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity；它背后的词干是希腊语里表示「琥珀」的词。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus and electricity were coined later by scientists.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 有记录；electricus 与 electricity 是后来由科学家造出的。

items.example: It carried the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: It was coined in the seventeenth century.

definition_zh: 电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的
definition_en: working by controlling the flow of electrons in circuits, using computer or network technology, made with synthesizers, or relating to the science of electronics
core_image: 电路板上密布芯片与细如发丝的走线，指示灯一闪一闪
scene: 超市收银台前，顾客把手机贴在读卡器上，滴一声就完成了付款。Most shops now accept electronic payment.
sceneCN: 这里 electronic 是「电子化的、用电子手段完成的」（第 2 个义项：借助计算机与网络技术）；句意是多数商店现在都接受电子支付。

pos.zh: 形容词：电子的；电子设备的；电子化的；电子音乐的；电子学的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ic 得到，义为「电子」
由本词加 -s 构成，义为「电子学；电子器件」
由本词加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「用电子方式地」
由本词加 -ian 构成，义为「电子工程师」

senses.title: Working through circuits
senses.titleCN: 电子的；靠电子电路工作的
senses.definition: operating by controlling the movement of electrons through circuits such as transistors and chips
senses.definitionCN: 通过控制电子在晶体管、芯片等电路中流动来工作
senses.example: The lab is testing a new electronic circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室正在测试一块新的电子电路。
senses.why: The suffix -ic turns the particle name into an adjective, so the word describes anything that works by steering electrons.
senses.whyCN: -ic 词尾把粒子名变成形容词，于是这个词形容一切靠操控电子来工作的东西。

senses.title: Done by computer or network
senses.titleCN: 电子化的；用电子手段完成的
senses.definition: carried out using computers, networks or digital systems rather than paper or face-to-face contact
senses.definitionCN: 借助计算机、网络或数字系统完成，而不是纸面或面对面
senses.example: Most shops now accept electronic payment.
senses.exampleCN: 多数商店现在都接受电子支付。
senses.why: Once a whole transaction runs through chips and networks, the device adjective spreads to the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 当一笔交易整个跑在芯片与网络上，指设备的形容词就扩展到了活动本身。

senses.title: Made with synthesizers
senses.definition: of music produced with synthesizers, samplers and other electronic instruments
senses.definitionCN: 用合成器、采样器及其他电子乐器制作的音乐
senses.example: She writes electronic music on a laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在笔记本电脑上写电子音乐。
senses.why: The instruments are the style, so the adjective naming the technology ended up naming a whole genre.
senses.whyCN: 乐器就是风格本身，于是命名这项技术的形容词最后成了一个音乐流派的名称。

senses.title: Of the science of electronics
senses.definition: relating to electronics as a branch of engineering and physics
senses.definitionCN: 指作为工程学与物理学分支的电子学
senses.example: He teaches electronic engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 他教电子工程。
senses.why: The field that studies these circuits needed a name, and the adjective before engineering supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 研究这些电路的那门学科需要名字，而 engineering 前面的这个形容词正好提供了它。

intro.en: Electronic is electron plus -ic, coined once the particle had been found; the root itself is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加 -ic，在粒子被发现之后才造出；而这个词根本身是希腊语里的「琥珀」。

items.en: Elektron named amber, whose rubbed surface first showed attraction.
items.cn: elektron 指琥珀，摩擦后的表面最先显现出吸引现象。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and passed the root into modern science.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 electrum 表示琥珀，并把这个词根传进近代科学。

items.en: The particle name electron gave the family a solid centre.
items.cn: 粒子名 electron 为这个词族提供了坚实的中心。

items.en: Valves and then transistors made a new adjective necessary for circuits.
items.cn: 电子管以及后来的晶体管，使指电路的形容词成为必需。

items.en: The -ic form covered devices, then transactions, then music.
items.cn: 加 -ic 的形式先指设备，再指交易，最后指音乐。

items.en: Electronic now names a whole layer of daily life built on chips.
items.cn: 如今 electronic 命名了建立在芯片之上的整整一层日常生活。

note.en: The look-alike group lines up the electric family; the near-meaning group separates electronic from electric, digital and electrical.
note.cn: 形近组排开 electric 词族；近义组区分 electronic 与 electric、digital、electrical。

entries.definition: The negative particle that these circuits control.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子」，正是这些电路所控制的粒子。

entries.definition: The science of such circuits, or the circuits as goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子学」，也指作为商品的电子器件。

entries.definition: By electronic means.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「用电子方式地」。

entries.definition: Of wiring and power systems rather than of chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，指布线供电系统而非芯片。

entries.definition: Driven by electricity in the plain sense, as a kettle or a motor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「用电的」，指水壶、马达这类普通用电的东西。

entries.definition: Stored as numbers; overlaps the network sense but says nothing about circuits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「数字的」，与网络义重叠，但不涉及电路。

entries.definition: Belonging to the power system, a wider and older field.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电气的」，属于更宽、更早的电力领域。

entries.definition: Run by machines; close to the transaction sense but not tied to chips.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自动化的」，接近交易义，但不限于芯片。

normalIntro.en: These hooks walk from a single electron to a chip, then to a payment, a track and a degree.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一个电子走到一块芯片，再走到一笔支付、一首曲子与一个学位。

normal.en: One electron is a particle; electronic is a whole way of working.
normal.cn: 一个电子是粒子；electronic 则是一整套工作方式。

normal.en: Electric kettles heat; electronic devices decide.
normal.cn: electric 水壶负责加热；electronic 设备负责判断。

normal.en: Electronic mail is mail without paper.
normal.cn: electronic mail 就是没有纸的邮件。

normal.en: Electronic music is music without a visible instrument.
normal.cn: electronic music 就是看不见乐器的音乐。

normal.en: A chip is a city of electrons with traffic rules.
normal.cn: 一块芯片就是一座有交通规则的电子之城。

abstract.en: Picture a circuit board as an aerial map of a small city at night.
abstract.cn: 把电路板想成夜里一座小城市的航拍图。

abstract.en: Electrons are the traffic; the chip is the road plan.
abstract.cn: 电子是车流；芯片是道路规划。

abstract.en: Electronic is what happens when the smallest particle is put in charge of the biggest systems.
abstract.cn: electronic 就是最小的粒子掌管最大系统时发生的事。

examples.en: The lab is testing a new electronic circuit.
examples.cn: 实验室正在测试一块新的电子电路。

examples.en: Most shops now accept electronic payment.
examples.cn: 多数商店现在都接受电子支付。

examples.en: She writes electronic music on a laptop.
examples.cn: 她在笔记本电脑上写电子音乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗来克胀尼克」——芯片上密密麻麻的走线一起闪，机器就活了

root: 由 electron 加形容词词尾 -ic 构成；electron 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 进入英语科学词汇。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of electronic: circuits, computer-based activities, synth music, and the engineering field.
sensesIntro.cn: electronic 的四个义项：电子电路、依托计算机的活动、合成器音乐，以及电子工程学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chip with hair-thin tracks and a blinking indicator light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块芯片，走线细如发丝，指示灯一闪一闪。

branches.en: THE CIRCUIT: electrons steered by transistors and chips.
branches.cn: 电路线：由晶体管与芯片操控的电子。

branches.en: THE TRANSACTION: money and mail moved through networks.
branches.cn: 交易线：透过网络转移的钱与邮件。

branches.en: THE GENRE: a style named after its instruments.
branches.cn: 流派线：以乐器命名的一种音乐风格。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the engineering that designs the circuits.
branches.cn: 学科线：设计这些电路的工程学。

branches.en: THE CHIP: every paperless payment is a chip doing arithmetic.
branches.cn: 芯片线：每一笔无纸支付，都是芯片在做算术。

intro.en: Electronic is electron with the adjective suffix -ic; the root behind both is the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加形容词词尾 -ic；两者背后的词根都是希腊语的「琥珀」。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are the older recorded forms; electron and electronic are modern coinages.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 是较早的有记录形式；electron 与 electronic 都是现代造词。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family.
It supplies the stem of this word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了这个词的词干。

definition_zh: 元素；（构成整体的）要素；成分；少量；[the elements] 恶劣天气
definition_en: a simple chemical substance that cannot be split by chemical means, one part of a whole, a small amount of a quality, or the forces of weather
core_image: 摊开的元素周期表，一格一格印着字母符号
scene: 老师在黑板上画了一张表格，一格一格写着字母和数字。Carbon is an element found in every living thing.
sceneCN: 这里 element 是「化学元素」（第 1 个义项：由同种原子构成、不能用化学方法再分的物质）；句意是碳是每个生物体内都能找到的元素。

pos.zh: 名词：元素；要素；成分；少量；[复数] 恶劣天气

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「基本的；自然力的；元素的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，义为「基础的；初级的」
由 elemental 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「基本地；以自然力地」

senses.title: A chemical element
senses.definition: a substance made of only one kind of atom, which cannot be broken down by chemical means
senses.definitionCN: 只由一种原子构成的物质，无法用化学方法再分
senses.example: Oxygen is the most common element in the earth's crust.
senses.exampleCN: 氧是地壳中含量最多的元素。
senses.why: Elementum first named a first principle, a unit you cannot go behind; chemistry kept exactly that role for the simplest substances.
senses.whyCN: elementum 最初指「不可再往前拆的第一原则」，化学把完全相同的角色留给了最简单的物质。

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: one of the parts or qualities that together make up a whole thing
senses.definitionCN: 共同构成某一整体的部分或性质之一
senses.example: Trust is a key element of any friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是任何友谊的关键要素。
senses.why: If an element is an irreducible unit, then a complex thing is merely a set of such units, so the word names any necessary part.
senses.whyCN: 既然 element 是不可再分的单位，复杂事物就只是一组这样的单位，于是这个词指任何必要的组成部分。

senses.title: A small amount of a quality
senses.definition: a small but noticeable amount of a quality or feeling within something larger
senses.definitionCN: 某个较大事物中少量却可察觉的性质或情绪
senses.example: There is an element of truth in what she says.
senses.exampleCN: 她说的话里有几分道理。
senses.why: The irreducible unit can be tiny, so an element became a small measure of something mixed in.
senses.whyCN: 不可再分的单位可以很小，于是 element 变成掺在其中的一点分量。

senses.title: Wind rain and cold
senses.definition: the forces of weather, especially bad weather, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 天气的力量，尤指恶劣天气，多用复数
senses.example: The tent kept out the elements.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶帐篷挡住了风吹雨打。
senses.why: The old four elements were earth, air, fire and water, and the open sky was thought to be their arena, so weather became the elements.
senses.whyCN: 古老的四元素是土、气、火、水，而开阔的天空被当作它们的战场，于是天气就成了 the elements。

intro.en: Element comes from Latin elementum, a word of debated origin meaning a first principle; note that the opening e- is part of the stem, not a prefix.
intro.cn: element 来自拉丁语 elementum，意为「第一原则」，其来源至今有争议；注意开头的 e- 属于词干本身，不是前缀。

items.en: Elementum named a first principle and also the letters of the alphabet, the units of writing.
items.cn: elementum 指第一原则，也指字母表里的字母，即书写的单位。

items.en: In the plural it named the four basic substances: earth, water, air and fire.
items.cn: 复数形式指四种基本物质：土、水、气、火。

items.en: French kept the word for a basic component of anything.
items.cn: 法语保留这个词，指任何事物的基本组成部分。

items.en: English used it for the four substances and for the parts of a whole.
items.cn: 英语用它指四种元素，也指整体的各个部分。

items.en: With modern chemistry the word was fixed to substances defined by atomic number.
items.cn: 随着近代化学的发展，这个词被固定给按原子序数定义的物质。

items.en: The weather sense survives in the plural, the quality sense in phrases like an element of truth.
items.cn: 天气义留在复数中，性质义留在 an element of truth 这类短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the element family; the near-meaning group separates a component, an ingredient, a factor and a substance.
note.cn: 形近组收 element 词族；近义组区分 component、ingredient、factor 与 substance。

entries.definition: Of the elements or of raw natural forces; basic and powerful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基本的；自然力的」，带原始力量感。

entries.definition: At the simplest level; also the adjective for basic particles.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基础的；初级的」，也用于基本粒子。

entries.definition: The plural, used for weather or for a set of basic parts.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指恶劣天气或一组基本组成部分。

entries.definition: A part of a machine or system; more technical than element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部件、组件」，比 element 更技术化。

entries.definition: One of the things mixed into a recipe or a product.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成分、配料」，指混进配方或产品里的东西。

entries.definition: One thing that influences a result; about causes rather than parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「因素」，指影响结果的原因，而非组成的部分。

entries.definition: A material with a definite make-up; the physical side of the chemical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物质」，是元素义在物理层面的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word close to its Latin sense of a unit you cannot break, then spread that unit across chemistry, wholes and weather.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子让词义贴近拉丁语「拆不开的单位」，再把单位铺到化学、整体与天气上。

normal.en: The e- in element is not a prefix; elementum is one solid stem.
normal.cn: element 开头的 e- 不是前缀，elementum 整个是实心词干。

normal.en: A chemical element is the last stop: split it and it is no longer that element.
normal.cn: 化学 element 是终点：再分下去，它就不是那个元素了。

normal.en: An element of a plan is one brick that cannot be left out.
normal.cn: 计划里的一个 element，就是一块不能少的砖。

normal.en: An element of truth is a small piece that cannot be split further.
normal.cn: an element of truth 就是一粒再拆不开的真话。

normal.en: The weather outside is the elements because the sky was their arena.
normal.cn: 外面的天气叫 the elements，因为天空曾是四元素的战场。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every cell holds one letter and one number.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，每一格只装一个字母和一个数字。

abstract.en: Everything complicated is a stack of these single cells.
abstract.cn: 一切复杂的东西，都是这些单格堆起来的。

abstract.en: Element is the smallest block that still keeps its own name.
abstract.cn: element 是仍然保有自己名字的最小一块。

examples.en: Oxygen is the most common element in the earth's crust.
examples.cn: 氧是地壳中含量最多的元素。

examples.en: Trust is a key element of any friendship.
examples.cn: 信任是任何友谊的关键要素。

examples.en: There is an element of truth in what she says.
examples.cn: 她说的话里有几分道理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒门特」——元素周期表一格一格，每格只住一个住户

root: 源自拉丁语 elementum「第一原则；字母」，来源有争议；开头的 e- 不是前缀，而是词干的一部分，与 elevate 的 e-（＝ex-）不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of element: the chemical substance, a necessary part, a small amount of a quality, and the weather in the plural.
sensesIntro.cn: element 的四个义项：化学元素、必要组成部分、少量的某种性质，以及复数形式的恶劣天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a periodic table whose cells each hold one letter and one number.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张周期表，每格只装一个字母和一个数字。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: one kind of atom, named by number.
branches.cn: 物质线：一种原子，以序数命名。

branches.en: THE PART: a unit that a whole cannot do without.
branches.cn: 部分线：整体少不了的那个单位。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the same unit shrunk to a hint.
branches.cn: 微量线：同一个单位缩小成一缕线索。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: the old four elements turned into sky.
branches.cn: 天气线：古老的四元素化作头顶的天空。

branches.en: THE TABLE: chemistry and plain parts share one word.
branches.cn: 表格线：化学与日常的「部分」共用一个词。

intro.en: Element has no prefix: the whole word is the Latin stem elementum, and the -ment at the end is a worn-down ending rather than the English suffix.
intro.cn: element 没有前缀：整个词就是拉丁词干 elementum，末尾的 -ment 是磨损后的词尾，不是英语后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: Elementum and its plural elementa are recorded Latin forms; the word's deeper origin is still disputed.
latinIntro.cn: elementum 及其复数 elementa 是有记录的拉丁语形式；这个词更深的来源至今仍有争议。

items.example: It is the whole stem of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它就是这个词的整个词干。

items.example: It is borrowed with little change.
items.exampleCN: 它几乎未经改动被借入。

items.meaningCN: 磨损的拉丁词尾，并非后缀
items.example: It is not the -ment of movement.
items.exampleCN: 它不是 movement 里的那个 -ment。

derivatives.zh: 基本的；自然力的；元素的

definition_zh: 电梯；升降机；升降舵；谷物提升机
definition_en: a machine in a building that carries people or goods between floors, a movable flap on an aircraft tail, or a machine that lifts grain
core_image: 金属轿厢沿着一列井道灯缓缓上升，楼层数字一格一格跳
scene: 酒店大堂里，穿制服的服务生替客人按住门，轿厢稳稳停住。The elevator stopped at the fourteenth floor.
sceneCN: 这里 elevator 是「电梯」（第 1 个义项：在楼层之间运送人或货的机器）；句意是电梯停在了十四层。

pos.zh: 名词：电梯；升降机；升降舵；谷物提升机

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -or 得到，义为「举起；提高」
由 elevate 加 -ion 构成，义为「海拔；提升」
由 elevate 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「升高的；高雅的」

senses.title: A machine between floors
senses.definition: a cage or platform in a building that carries people or goods up and down between floors
senses.definitionCN: 建筑中在楼层之间运送人或货的轿厢或平台
senses.example: The elevator stopped at the fourteenth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯停在了十四层。
senses.why: The -or ending names the thing that does the verb, so elevator is literally the lifter, and the machine that lifts became the word.
senses.whyCN: -or 词尾命名做这个动作的东西，所以 elevator 字面就是「举升者」，负责举升的机器便得了这个名字。

senses.title: A flap on the tail
senses.definition: a hinged control surface on the tailplane of an aircraft that makes the nose go up or down
senses.definitionCN: 飞机水平尾翼上可转动的操纵面，使机头抬起或低下
senses.example: The pilot pushed the elevator down and the nose dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员推下升降舵，机头随即下沉。
senses.why: The flap literally lifts or lowers the nose, so aviation reused the same agent noun for the part that does it.
senses.whyCN: 这块舵面确实在抬起或压低机头，于是航空业把同一个施动名词用在了做这件事的部件上。

senses.title: A grain lifter
senses.definition: a tall building or machine that lifts and stores grain in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 把谷物大批提升并储存的高塔或机械
senses.example: The grain was trucked to the elevator beside the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物被卡车运到铁路旁的谷物提升机。
senses.why: Farm machinery needed a plain name for a machine that raises grain, and the oldest sense of lift fitted exactly.
senses.whyCN: 农业机械需要给「把谷物举高」的机器一个朴素名称，而 lift 最古老的含义正合适。

intro.en: Elevator is elevate plus the Latin agent ending -or, so it means the lifter; American English applied it to the machine, while British English kept lift.
intro.cn: elevator 是 elevate 加拉丁语施动词尾 -or，意为「举升者」；美式英语把它用在机器上，英式英语则保留 lift。

items.en: Levare meant to lighten and to raise, built on levis, light in weight.
items.cn: levare 意为使轻、举起，其根是 levis（轻的）。

items.en: With the prefix ex- it became elevare, to lift up and out.
items.cn: 加上前缀 ex- 后成为 elevare，意为向上抬起。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词。

items.en: The agent ending -or made a noun meaning one that lifts.
items.cn: 施动词尾 -or 造出意为「举升者」的名词。

items.en: American English fixed the word on the passenger machine in tall buildings.
items.cn: 美式英语把这个词固定给高层建筑里的载人机器。

items.en: British lift and American elevator now name the same box, and aviation took the word for a tail flap.
items.cn: 英式 lift 与美式 elevator 如今指同一只轿厢，航空业又借它命名尾翼舵面。

note.en: The look-alike group links the elevate family; the near-meaning group separates lift, escalator and hoist.
note.cn: 形近组串起 elevate 词族；近义组区分 lift、escalator 与 hoist。

entries.definition: The verb that the noun is built from.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「举起；提高」，是本词的基干。

entries.definition: Height above sea level, or the act of raising.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海拔；提升」。

entries.definition: Raised, or noble in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升高的；高雅的」。

entries.definition: A bar for lifting, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杠杆」，与 elevator 同根。

entries.definition: The British word for the same machine; also a general verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电梯」，是英式说法，也可作一般动词。

entries.definition: A moving staircase, not a box; it carries you step by step.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自动扶梯」，是移动的楼梯而非轿厢。

entries.definition: A rope or machine for lifting heavy loads, usually outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起重机、卷扬机」，多用于室外吊重物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read the word as lift plus the doer, then follow that doer into a shaft, a tail and a grain tower.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把词读成「举起＋做这事的东西」，再让这个「做者」走进井道、机尾与谷仓塔。

normal.en: Elevate plus -or: the thing that lifts.
normal.cn: elevate 加 -or：负责举升的那个东西。

normal.en: In Britain the same box is simply called a lift.
normal.cn: 在英国，同一只轿厢就直接叫 lift。

normal.en: An elevator pitch is short enough to finish between floors.
normal.cn: elevator pitch 短到能在楼层之间讲完。

normal.en: On a plane the elevator lifts the nose, not the cabin.
normal.cn: 飞机上的 elevator 抬起的是机头，不是客舱。

normal.en: A grain elevator lifts wheat into a tower.
normal.cn: grain elevator 把小麦提升进高塔。

abstract.en: Picture a small metal room that refuses to stay on one floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小金属房间，就是不肯停在同一层。

abstract.en: The same name serves a tail flap and a grain tower, because all three raise something.
abstract.cn: 同一个名字兼指尾翼舵面与谷物塔，因为三者都在抬高什么。

abstract.en: Elevator is the verb elevate given a body.
abstract.cn: elevator 就是动词 elevate 被赋予了一具身体。

examples.en: The elevator stopped at the fourteenth floor.
examples.cn: 电梯停在了十四层。

examples.en: The pilot pushed the elevator down and the nose dropped.
examples.cn: 飞行员推下升降舵，机头随即下沉。

examples.en: The grain was trucked to the elevator beside the railway.
examples.cn: 谷物被卡车运到铁路旁的谷物提升机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒维特」——轿厢一升，楼层数字就跳一格

root: 由 elevate 加拉丁语施动词尾 -or 构成，字面意为「举升者」；elevate 出自 elevare，即前缀 e-（＝ex-）加 levare「使轻、举起」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elevator: the machine in a building, the tail flap of an aircraft, and the machine that lifts grain.
sensesIntro.cn: elevator 的三个义项：建筑里的电梯、飞机的升降舵，以及提升谷物的机械。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal box climbing a shaft, floor numbers ticking upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只金属轿厢沿井道上升，楼层数字一跳一跳。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: people and goods moving between floors.
branches.cn: 建筑线：在楼层之间运送人与货。

branches.en: THE AIRCRAFT: a flap that tilts the nose.
branches.cn: 航空线：让机头俯仰的舵面。

branches.en: THE FARM: grain raised into a tower.
branches.cn: 农业线：把谷物提升进高塔。

branches.en: THE LIFT: a shaft for people and a shaft for wheat.
branches.cn: 举升线：送人的井道与送麦的塔都叫这个名字。

branches.en: THE CONTROL: one is controlled by buttons, one by a stick.
branches.cn: 操控线：一个靠按钮，一个靠操纵杆。

intro.en: Elevator is elevate plus the Latin agent ending -or, so its shape says one that lifts; the e- inside elevate is the real prefix ex-.
intro.cn: elevator 是 elevate 加拉丁语施动词尾 -or，字形本身就在说「举升者」；elevate 内部的 e- 是真正的前缀 ex-。

latinIntro.en: Levare and elevare are recorded Latin verbs; the agent noun elevator is a later English formation.
latinIntro.cn: levare 与 elevare 是有记录的拉丁语动词；施动名词 elevator 则是后来英语的构造。

It drops -or to give the verb.

definition_zh: 别的；其他的；另外；否则
definition_en: other or different; in addition; otherwise
core_image: 手伸向另一个抽屉，那里放着不一样的东西
scene: 抽屉翻遍了也没找到，孩子又问起别的可能。She looked in every drawer and asked if there was anything else.
sceneCN: 这里 else 是「别的、其他的」（第 01 个义项：不同于已提到的事物）；句意是她翻遍抽屉，问还有没有别的东西。

pos.zh: 副词：别的；另外；否则
形容词（后置）：其他的

derivatives.zh: 由 else 与 where 复合，义为「在别处」
由 else 加 -wise 构成，义为「以别的方式」（少见）

senses.title: Other than what was mentioned
senses.definition: different from the thing already mentioned, used after words such as something or anyone
senses.definitionCN: 不同于已经提到的事物，常用于 something、anyone 等词之后
senses.example: She looked in every drawer and asked if there was anything else.
senses.exampleCN: 她翻遍抽屉，问还有没有别的东西。
senses.why: Old English elles meant in another way, so else points away from the thing just named and toward a different one.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 elles 意为「以另一种方式」，所以 else 把注意力从刚提到的东西上移开，指向不一样的另一个。

senses.title: An additional person or thing
senses.definition: in addition to the people or things already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在已经提到的人或物之外再加一个
senses.example: Who else came to the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 还有谁来参加了会议？
senses.why: Asking who else means asking for one more name beyond the known list, so the different-thing sense also serves as an addition.
senses.whyCN: 问 who else 就是问已知名单之外再多一个名字，于是「不同的东西」这一层意思也用来表示追加。

senses.title: Otherwise, as a warning
senses.definition: used after or to introduce a bad result if something is not done
senses.definitionCN: 用在 or 之后或句首，引出若不照做就会发生的坏结果
senses.example: Hurry up, or else we will miss the train.
senses.exampleCN: 快点，否则我们会赶不上火车。
senses.why: The alternative way is presented as a threat, so else moves from another option to another, worse outcome.
senses.whyCN: 另一条路被摆成威胁，于是 else 从「另一个选项」滑向「另一个更糟的结果」。

intro.en: Else is an old Germanic adverb meaning in another way, related to the idea of other rather than to the modern word also.
intro.cn: else 是古老的日耳曼语副词，意为「以另一种方式」，与「其他」的观念相关，而不是来自现代的 also。

items.en: A root reconstructed as al- carried the sense of other.
items.cn: 可重构的 al- 词根带有「其他」的意思。

items.en: The adverb took the form alljas, still meaning otherwise.
items.cn: 这个副词作 alljas，仍表示「以另一种方式」。

items.en: It appears as elles in Old English texts.
items.cn: 在古英语文献中写作 elles。

items.en: Spelling settled toward els and then else.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写先固定为 els，再演变为 else。

items.en: The adverb was fixed after indefinite pronouns, giving something else and anyone else.
items.cn: 现代英语把它固定在不定代词之后，形成 something else 与 anyone else。

note.en: The look-alike group shows compounds and derivatives built on else; the near-meaning group compares other, otherwise and additional.
note.cn: 形近组展示由 else 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组则比较 other、otherwise 与「另外」。

entries.definition: In or to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「在别处、到别处」。

entries.definition: In another way, a rare synonym of otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以别的方式」，是 otherwise 的少见同义词。

entries.definition: A phrase introducing a warning or alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「否则」，用来引出警告或另一种选择。

entries.definition: A different person or thing from the one mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或代词，义为「其他的」，与 else 的核心义接近。

entries.definition: In different circumstances, or if not.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「否则、在其他情况下」。

entries.definition: One more, added to what already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的」，对应 else 的追加义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat else as the pointer to another drawer, then let it add one more name or warn about a worse outcome.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 else 当成指向另一个抽屉的手指，再让它追加一个名字或警告更糟的结果。

normal.en: Else means the other one, not this one.
normal.cn: else 指的是另一个，而不是眼前这个。

normal.en: Something else is a different thing.
normal.cn: something else 就是别的东西。

normal.en: Who else asks for one more name.
normal.cn: who else 就是再问一个名字。

normal.en: Or else introduces the bad alternative.
normal.cn: or else 引出糟糕的另一种结果。

normal.en: Elsewhere puts the same idea in another place.
normal.cn: elsewhere 把同一个意思放到另一个地方。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing past the open drawer to the next one.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手越过打开的抽屉，指向下一个。

abstract.en: The word always looks away from what is already known.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是把目光从已知的东西上移开。

abstract.en: One small word can add a name or threaten a loss.
abstract.cn: 一个短短的词，既能追加名字，也能威胁损失。

examples.en: She looked in every drawer and asked if there was anything else.
examples.cn: 她翻遍抽屉，问还有没有别的东西。

examples.en: Who else came to the meeting?
examples.cn: 还有谁来参加了会议？

examples.en: Hurry up, or else we will miss the train.
examples.cn: 快点，否则我们会赶不上火车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔斯」——爱找别的，这个不行就换另一个

root: 古英语 elles，意为「以另一种方式、在别处」，源于日耳曼语 alljas，与 other 的「另一」观念同源。

sensesIntro.en: Else points to a different thing, then to one more thing, then to a worse alternative.
sensesIntro.cn: else 先指向不一样的东西，再指向再加一个，最后指向更糟的另一种结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing away from the known drawer toward another one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指从已知的抽屉移开，指向另一个。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENT ONE: not this, but another.
branches.cn: 不同线：不是这个，而是另一个。

branches.en: THE EXTRA ONE: one more name on the list.
branches.cn: 追加线：名单上再多一个名字。

branches.en: THE WARNING: the other outcome is worse.
branches.cn: 警告线：另一个结果是更糟的。

branches.en: OTHER AND MORE: a different item can also be an extra one.
branches.cn: 另与再：不同的东西也可以是在原有之外再添一个。

branches.en: CHOICE AND THREAT: the alternative becomes a consequence.
branches.cn: 选择与威胁：另一种选择变成了后果。

intro.en: Else is a free adverb that mostly combines with where and wise rather than taking a classical prefix.
intro.cn: else 是一个自由副词，主要与 where、wise 组合，而不是接古典前缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin etymon, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语层，没有拉丁语词源，因此拉丁列表为空。

items.example: It is the base of the family.
It warns of a bad result.
It places else after an indefinite pronoun.
items.exampleCN: 它把 else 放在不定代词之后。

items.example: It is one of the commonest collocations.
items.exampleCN: 它是最常见的搭配之一。

definition_zh: 在别处；到别处；在其他地方
definition_en: in or to another place; in other places generally
core_image: 目光越过眼前这块地方，落在远处的另一片区域
scene: 聚会散场后，主人把多余的椅子搬到别处。The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
sceneCN: 这里 elsewhere 是「到别处」（第 01 个义项：到另一个地方）；句意是聚会结束后多余的椅子被搬到了别处。

pos.zh: 副词：在别处；到别处；在其他地方

derivatives.zh: 复合成分，义为「别的」，与 where 合成 elsewhere
复合成分，义为「哪里」，与 else 合成 elsewhere

senses.title: In or to another place
senses.definition: in or to a different place from the one already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在或到一个不同于已提及地点的地方
senses.example: The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会结束后，多余的椅子被搬到了别处。
senses.why: Else supplies the idea of another and where supplies place, so elsewhere is simply the place that is not here.
senses.whyCN: else 提供「另一个」的意思，where 提供「地方」，所以 elsewhere 就是那个不在这里的地方。

senses.title: In other places in general
senses.definition: in other places, considered as a group rather than one specific place
senses.definitionCN: 泛指其他多个地方，而不是某一个具体地点
senses.example: Elsewhere in Europe, the rule is stricter.
senses.exampleCN: 在欧洲其他地方，这条规定更严格。
senses.why: The same compound can widen from one other place to any other place, so the word also serves as a general contrast.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合词可以从「另一个地方」扩大到「任何其他地方」，于是它也用来作总体对比。

senses.title: In another source or part of a text
senses.titleCN: 在别处（指其他来源或篇章）
senses.definition: in another part of a book, report or set of records
senses.definitionCN: 在同一本书、报告或记录的其他部分
senses.example: The report refers elsewhere for the full figures.
senses.exampleCN: 完整数据报告让读者去别处查看。
senses.why: A text is treated as a space with places, so a cross-reference sends the reader to a different spot in that space.
senses.whyCN: 文本被当成一个有地点可走的空间，于是交叉引用就是把读者送到这个空间里的另一处。

intro.en: Elsewhere is a transparent compound of else and where, already present in Old English.
intro.cn: elsewhere 是 else 与 where 的透明复合词，古英语中已经存在。

items.en: The compound appears as elleshwær, meaning in another place.
items.cn: 古英语作 elleshwær，意为「在另一个地方」。

items.en: Spelling passed through elleswhere and elsquer.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写经过 elleswhere、elsquer 等形式。

items.en: Printing helped fix the modern spelling elsewhere.
items.cn: 印刷术帮助固定了现代拼写 elsewhere。

items.en: The word extended from physical places to sources and parts of texts.
items.cn: 这个词从物理地点扩展到资料来源与文本部分。

items.en: It is now a standard adverb in news, law and academic writing.
items.cn: 如今它是新闻、法律与学术写作中的标准副词。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the else and where building blocks; the near-meaning group places elsewhere among other place words.
note.cn: 形近组展示 else 与 where 这两块构件；近义组把 elsewhere 放进其他地点词中比较。

entries.definition: The other element that supplies the idea of another.
entries.definitionCN: 复合成分，提供「另一个」的意思。

entries.definition: The element that supplies place.
entries.definitionCN: 复合成分，提供「地方」的意思。

entries.definition: In all places, built with the same place element.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带 -where 的地点词，义为「到处」。

entries.definition: In or to an unspecified place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在某处」，地点同样不确定。

entries.definition: In or to a foreign country.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在国外」，是 elsewhere 的一种具体化。

entries.definition: At a distance from the current place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「离开、在远处」，强调距离。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split elsewhere into else plus where, then move the reader from one room to another.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 elsewhere 拆成 else 加 where，再把读者从一个房间带到另一个房间。

normal.en: Else plus where means the other place.
normal.cn: else 加 where 就是「另一个地方」。

normal.en: If it is not here, look elsewhere.
normal.cn: 如果不在这里，就到别处找。

normal.en: Elsewhere in Europe marks a wider contrast.
normal.cn: elsewhere in Europe 表示更大范围的对比。

normal.en: A cross-reference sends you elsewhere in the book.
normal.cn: 交叉引用把你送到书里的别处。

normal.en: Everywhere and somewhere share the same -where.
normal.cn: everywhere 与 somewhere 都带同一个 -where。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight leaving this room and landing on another.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯离开这个房间，落到另一个房间。

abstract.en: The word is a small map with only two points: here and not here.
abstract.cn: 这个词像一张只有两个点的小地图：这里，和不在这里。

abstract.en: A footnote is elsewhere made visible.
abstract.cn: 脚注就是被标出来的「别处」。

examples.en: The extra chairs were carried elsewhere after the party.
examples.cn: 聚会结束后，多余的椅子被搬到了别处。

examples.en: Elsewhere in Europe, the rule is stricter.
examples.cn: 在欧洲其他地方，这条规定更严格。

examples.en: The report refers elsewhere for the full figures.
examples.cn: 完整数据报告让读者去别处查看。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱尔斯维尔」——不是这儿，是别的哪儿

root: 由 else（别的）与 where（哪里）复合而成，古英语作 elleshwær，字面就是「在另一个地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Elsewhere begins as one other place, widens to other places in general, and then enters texts as another source.
sensesIntro.cn: elsewhere 从某一个别处开始，扩大到泛指其他地方，再进入文本表示另一个出处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gaze sliding past the present spot to a distant one.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光越过眼前的位置，滑向远处另一处。

branches.en: THE OTHER SPOT: a specific place that is not here.
branches.cn: 另一处：一个具体但不在这里的地点。

branches.en: THE WIDER WORLD: other places taken together.
branches.cn: 更广的世界：把其他地方合起来看。

branches.en: THE TEXT: another page or source.
branches.cn: 文本线：另一页或另一个来源。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: one other place can widen into many.
branches.cn: 一与多：一个别处可以扩大成许多别处。

branches.en: SPACE AND PAGE: a place word becomes a reading direction.
branches.cn: 空间与书页：地点词变成了阅读方向。

intro.en: Elsewhere is a compound of two free morphemes, else and where, with no classical prefix.
intro.cn: elsewhere 由 else 与 where 两个自由语素复合而成，没有古典前缀。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic, so there is no Latin entry to list.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都属于日耳曼语层，因此没有可列的拉丁词条。

items.example: It appears in everywhere and somewhere.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 everywhere 与 somewhere 中。
它由 else 与 where 合成。

definition_zh: 电子邮件；电子邮件系统；发电子邮件
definition_en: a message sent electronically over a network; the email system; to send such a message
core_image: 一封信化作光点，沿着看不见的线飞进对方的屏幕
scene: 地铁进站前，她低头用手机回完了最后一封信。She checked her email before the train arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 email 是「电子邮件」（第 01 个义项：通过网络发送的电子信件）；句意是列车到站前她查看了邮件。

pos.zh: 名词：电子邮件；电子邮件系统
及物动词：发电子邮件

derivatives.zh: 由 electronic mail 简化而来的基础词，义为「邮件」
带连字符的旧式拼写，义同 email
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「发邮件的人或邮件程序」

senses.title: A message sent over a network
senses.definition: a written message sent from one computer or phone to another through the internet
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网从一台电脑或手机发送到另一台的书面信息
senses.example: She checked her email before the train arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 列车到站前她查看了邮件。
senses.why: The word joins electronic and mail, so an old paper letter keeps its name while its body turns into data travelling through wires.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 electronic 与 mail 合成，纸信的名字被保留下来，但信的内容变成了沿线路传输的数据。

senses.title: The email system
senses.definition: the whole system of accounts, servers and software used to send such messages
senses.definitionCN: 用来发送这类信息的账号、服务器与软件构成的整套系统
senses.example: The company moved all its email to the cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把所有邮件系统都迁移到了云端。
senses.why: A single message and the network that carries it share one name, so email also means the postal system of the internet.
senses.whyCN: 单封邮件与承载它的网络共用一个名字，所以 email 也指互联网上的那套邮政系统。

senses.title: To send an email
senses.definition: to send a message to someone using email
senses.definitionCN: 用电子邮件给某人发送信息
senses.example: Please email me the draft by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前把草稿发邮件给我。
senses.why: Any mail noun in English can turn into a verb meaning to send it, so email follows mail and letter into action.
senses.whyCN: 英语里凡是「邮件」类名词都能转成表示「寄送」的动词，email 于是跟着 mail 一起从物品变成了动作。

intro.en: Email is a twentieth-century compound of electronic and mail, with mail itself coming from an old word for a bag.
intro.cn: email 是二十世纪由 electronic 与 mail 合成的词，而 mail 本身来自一个表示「袋子」的古老词。

items.en: Male meant a bag or bundle, especially a traveller's pack.
items.cn: 古法语 male 指袋子或包裹，尤指旅人的行囊。

items.en: English mail first meant a bag of letters, then the letters themselves.
items.cn: 中古英语 mail 先指一袋信件，后来指信件本身。

items.en: The postal sense became standard in Britain and America.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，邮政义在英美成为标准用法。

items.en: Computing coined electronic mail for messages passed between machines.
items.cn: 计算机领域造出 electronic mail，指机器之间传递的信息。

items.en: The clipped form email replaced the longer phrase and then became a verb.
items.cn: 缩略形式 email 取代了较长短语，随后又用作动词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the mail family; the near-meaning group separates a message, a paper letter and the place where mail waits.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 mail 词族展开；近义组区分一条信息、一封纸质信与收件的地方。

entries.definition: Letters and parcels sent by post, or the system that carries them.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「邮件、邮政」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: The older hyphenated spelling of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的旧式连字符拼写。

entries.definition: A box where mail is delivered or stored.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「信箱」，也可指电子邮箱。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, by any channel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消息」，可经任何渠道传递。

entries.definition: A written message on paper, usually posted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信件」，通常写在纸上邮寄。

entries.definition: The folder where incoming email is collected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收件箱」，是邮件到达后聚集的地方。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read email as electronic mail, then follow the letter into a message, a system and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 email 读成「电子的邮件」，再让这封信变成消息、系统与动作。

normal.en: Electronic plus mail gives email.
normal.cn: electronic 加 mail 就是 email。

normal.en: Mail first meant a bag of letters.
normal.cn: mail 最早指装信的一只袋子。

normal.en: An email address is the electronic version of a house address.
normal.cn: email address 就是电子版的门牌地址。

normal.en: You can email a file or a person.
normal.cn: 你可以把文件或人「邮件」一下，也就是发信给对象。

normal.en: The inbox is the mailbox of the screen.
normal.cn: 收件箱就是屏幕里的信箱。

abstract.en: Picture a paper letter dissolving into sparks that fly along a wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一封纸信化成火花，沿着线路飞走。

abstract.en: A message and the system that carries it wear the same name.
abstract.cn: 一条消息与承载它的系统穿着同一个名字。

abstract.en: The word is a post office squeezed into a screen.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一家被塞进屏幕的邮局。

examples.en: She checked her email before the train arrived.
examples.cn: 列车到站前她查看了邮件。

examples.en: The company moved all its email to the cloud.
examples.cn: 公司把所有邮件系统都迁移到了云端。

examples.en: Please email me the draft by Friday.
examples.cn: 请在周五前把草稿发邮件给我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊妹儿」——网络上飞来的电子信件

root: 由 electronic（电子的）与 mail（邮件）缩合而成；mail 出自古法语 male（袋子），原指一袋信件。

sensesIntro.en: Email names one electronic letter, then the whole electronic postal system, and finally the act of sending.
sensesIntro.cn: email 先指一封电子信件，再指整套电子邮政系统，最后指发送这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter turning into sparks and flying through a wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封信化作火花，沿着线路飞向远方。

branches.en: THE LETTER: one message arriving in a screen.
branches.cn: 信件线：一条消息抵达屏幕。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: accounts, servers and software as one post office.
branches.cn: 系统线：账号、服务器与软件合成一家邮局。

branches.en: THE ACTION: to send such a message.
branches.cn: 动作线：发送这样一条消息。

branches.en: ITEM AND NETWORK: one letter and the network that carries it.
branches.cn: 单件与网络：一封信和承载它的网络。

branches.en: THING AND ACT: the object becomes the verb.
branches.cn: 物与动作：名词转成动词。

intro.en: Email is a clipped compound: e- stands for electronic and mail supplies the postal meaning.
intro.cn: email 是缩合复合词：e- 代表 electronic，mail 提供邮政含义。

latinIntro.en: The mail part is Germanic through French, and there is no single Latin etymon for the compound.
latinIntro.cn: mail 这一部分经法语来自日耳曼语，整个复合词没有单一的拉丁词源。

items.example: It stands for electronic in email.
items.exampleCN: 它在 email 中代表 electronic。

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

items.exampleCN: 它由 mail 与 box 合成。

definition_zh: 使尴尬；使难堪；使为难；阻碍
definition_en: to make someone feel ashamed or awkward; to cause difficulty for someone or something
core_image: 被一道看不见的栏杆围住，进退都不自在
scene: 台上忽然忘词，他脸颊一下红到耳根。The long silence embarrassed the young speaker.
sceneCN: 这里 embarrass 是「使难堪」（第 01 个义项：让人感到羞愧不自在）；句意是长时间的沉默让年轻演讲者很难堪。

pos.zh: 及物动词：使尴尬；使难堪；使为难

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「尴尬；难堪」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「感到尴尬的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「令人尴尬的」

senses.title: To make someone feel awkward
senses.definition: to make a person feel ashamed, nervous or socially uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到羞愧、紧张或在人前不自在
senses.example: The long silence embarrassed the young speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间的沉默让年轻演讲者很难堪。
senses.why: The old verb meant to block or entangle, so the core picture is being caught behind a barrier with no easy way out, which is exactly how social awkwardness feels.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老动词原本表示阻挡、缠住，核心画面是被栏杆困住、找不到出口，这正是社交尴尬的感受。

senses.title: To put someone in a difficult position
senses.definition: to cause problems or difficulties for a person or organization
senses.definitionCN: 给个人或机构造成麻烦与困难
senses.example: The question embarrassed the government.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题让政府很为难。
senses.why: Being blocked is not only social but practical, so the same verb describes a person or body trapped by an awkward problem.
senses.whyCN: 被挡住不只是社交上的事，也可能是实际处境，于是同一个动词也形容人或机构被难题困住。

senses.title: To hamper or obstruct, in older use
senses.definition: to hinder or obstruct movement or progress, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 阻碍移动或进展，这是较旧且罕见的义项
senses.example: Fallen trees embarrassed the advance of the column.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树木阻碍了队伍前进。
senses.why: The earliest sense is physical obstruction, and the social sense grew from it; the old meaning survives mainly in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思就是物理上的阻挡，社交义由此长出；旧义如今主要残留在正式书面语里。

intro.en: Embarrass came through French from a verb meaning to bar in, so its oldest picture is a barrier, not a blush.
intro.cn: embarrass 经法语来自一个意为「用栏杆围住」的动词，所以它最古老的画面是障碍，而不是脸红。

items.en: Imbarrare meant to bar in, built on barra, a bar.
items.cn: imbarrare 意为用栏杆围住，其根是 barra（栏杆）。

items.en: Embarrasser carried the sense of blocking or entangling.
items.cn: embarrasser 带有阻挡、缠住的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb first for physical hindrance.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该动词，最初指物理上的阻碍。

items.en: The social sense of making someone uncomfortable became common.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，表示让人不自在的社交义变得常见。

items.en: Today the awkward sense dominates, while the obstructive sense is rare and formal.
items.cn: 今天尴尬义占主导，阻碍义则少见且正式。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the -ment, -ed and -ing family; the near-meaning group separates shame, humiliation and plain confusion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 -ment、-ed、-ing 词族展开；近义组区分羞愧、羞辱与单纯的困惑。

entries.definition: The feeling or cause of being embarrassed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「尴尬」或「令人尴尬的事」。

entries.definition: Feeling ashamed or awkward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感到尴尬的」。

entries.definition: Causing someone to feel awkward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人尴尬的」。

entries.definition: A painful feeling of having done something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「羞耻」，强调做错事后的痛苦。

entries.definition: To make someone feel foolish in front of others.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「羞辱」，强调当众让人丢脸。

entries.definition: To make someone unable to understand, without the shame.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使困惑」，不一定带有羞耻感。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read embarrass as being barred in, then let the barrier become social awkwardness and practical difficulty.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 embarrass 读成「被栏杆围住」，再让这道栏杆变成社交尴尬与实际困难。

normal.en: Em- plus bar- suggests being barred in.
normal.cn: em- 加 bar- 让人想到被栏杆围在里面。

normal.en: The old verb meant to obstruct.
normal.cn: 这个古老动词原本表示阻挡。

normal.en: A blush is a barrier you cannot walk around.
normal.cn: 脸红就是一道绕不过去的栏杆。

normal.en: Embarrassment is the noun, embarrassed the feeling.
normal.cn: embarrassment 是名词，embarrassed 是那种感受。

normal.en: An embarrassing question traps the person who must answer.
normal.cn: embarrassing question 把必须回答的人困住。

abstract.en: Picture a fence rising around a speaker in the middle of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者说到一半，四周忽然升起一圈栅栏。

abstract.en: The word begins as a physical block and ends as a social one.
abstract.cn: 这个词从物理阻挡开始，最后变成社交上的困住。

abstract.en: To embarrass is to hand someone a problem with no exit.
abstract.cn: 使某人尴尬，就是递给他一个没有出口的难题。

examples.en: The long silence embarrassed the young speaker.
examples.cn: 长时间的沉默让年轻演讲者很难堪。

examples.en: The question embarrassed the government.
examples.cn: 这个问题让政府很为难。

examples.en: Fallen trees embarrassed the advance of the column.
examples.cn: 倒下的树木阻碍了队伍前进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一摸白肉死」——当众被看见，恨不得钻地缝

root: 经法语 embarrasser 借入，源头为西班牙语或意大利语 imbarrare，由 in-（在内）加 barra（栏杆）构成，字面为「用栏杆围住」。

sensesIntro.en: Embarrass starts as a physical barrier, becomes a social trap, then a practical difficulty, and keeps its old obstructive sense in formal writing.
sensesIntro.cn: embarrass 从物理栏杆开始，变成社交困境，再变成实际难题，并在正式书面语里保留古老的阻碍义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fence closing around a person who cannot step out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈栏杆合拢，把人困在中间，无处可退。

branches.en: THE BLUSH: the social barrier closes in.
branches.cn: 脸红线：社交栏杆合拢。

branches.en: THE PROBLEM: a person or body trapped by difficulty.
branches.cn: 难题线：人或机构被困难困住。

branches.en: THE OLD BARRIER: physical obstruction in formal use.
branches.cn: 旧栏杆：正式用语中的物理阻碍。

branches.en: FEELING AND POSITION: awkwardness is a kind of trap.
branches.cn: 感受与处境：尴尬本身就是一种困住。

branches.en: INNER AND OUTER: the same block is felt inside or seen outside.
branches.cn: 内与外：同一道阻挡，或在心里感到，或在外面看见。

intro.en: Embarrass is a borrowed French verb, so its parts are historical rather than productive English affixes.
intro.cn: embarrass 是借入的法语动词，其组成部分是历史沉积，而不是能产的英语词缀。

latinIntro.en: The ultimate root is barra, a bar, which passed through Romance languages into French.
latinIntro.cn: 最终词根是 barra（栏杆），经罗曼语族进入法语。

items.example: It marks being put inside a barrier.
items.exampleCN: 它标记被放进栏杆之内。

items.example: It is the root of the barrier image.

items.exampleCN: 它共享同一个栏杆意象。

definition_zh: 出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出
definition_en: to come out from a hidden place; to become known; to come into existence; to survive a difficult period
core_image: 水面下的一团影子慢慢升起，终于露出水面
scene: 云层裂开，太阳从背后露出边缘。The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里 emerge 是「露出、出现」（第 01 个义项：从遮蔽处出来）；句意是太阳从云层后露出。

pos.zh: 不及物动词：出现；浮现；显露；脱颖而出

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「出现；兴起」
由动词加 -ent 构成，义为「新兴的；浮现的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「新兴的；正在出现的」

senses.title: To come out from a hidden place
senses.definition: to move out of water, darkness or another covering and become visible
senses.definitionCN: 从水中、暗处或其他遮盖物里出来并变得可见
senses.example: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳从云层后露出。
senses.why: The Latin verb joins e-, out, with mergere, to dip or sink, so the core picture is something rising out of the water into view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词由 e-（向外）与 mergere（浸入、下沉）组合，核心画面就是某物从水里升起、露出水面。

senses.title: To become known
senses.definition: to become known or apparent after being hidden or unclear
senses.definitionCN: 原本隐藏或不清晰的事情变得为人所知
senses.example: New facts emerged during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判过程中有新的情况显露出来。
senses.why: Facts can rise out of obscurity just as an object rises out of water, so the physical surfacing becomes a metaphor for disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 事实能像物体升出水面一样从模糊中浮现，于是这个物理动作变成了「真相显露」的比喻。

senses.title: To come into existence
senses.definition: to begin to exist or become established
senses.definitionCN: 开始存在或逐渐确立
senses.example: A new industry emerged in the coastal city.
senses.exampleCN: 一座新兴产业在这座沿海城市兴起。
senses.why: What rises into view did not exist for the observer before, so emergence also names the birth of a thing or trend.
senses.whyCN: 对观察者来说，升起并进入视野的东西此前并不存在，所以 emergence 也用来命名事物或趋势的诞生。

senses.title: To survive a difficult period
senses.definition: to come out of a difficult experience in a new or stronger position
senses.definitionCN: 从艰难经历中走出来，处于新的或更强的位置
senses.example: The small firm emerged stronger after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后这家小公司变得更强。
senses.why: Coming out of water is also coming out of danger, so the verb describes a person or group that survives a trial and steps into the open.
senses.whyCN: 从水里出来也意味着从危险中出来，所以这个动词形容人或群体熬过考验、走到开阔处。

intro.en: Emerge comes straight from Latin emergere, to rise out of a liquid.
intro.cn: emerge 直接来自拉丁语 emergere，意为从液体中升起。

items.en: Mergere meant to dip, plunge or sink.
items.cn: mergere 意为浸入、扎入或下沉。

items.en: With e-, out, the verb meant to rise out of water.
items.cn: 加上 e-（向外）后，动词意为从水中升起。

items.en: The participle described something coming up into view.
items.cn: 其分词形容某物升上来、进入视野。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for physical surfacing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该动词，表示物理上的浮出。

items.en: The sense widened to facts becoming known and new things coming into being.
items.cn: 词义扩大到事实显露与新事物产生。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the merge root and its derived nouns; the near-meaning group separates appearing, surfacing and arising.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 merge 词根及其派生名词展开；近义组区分出现、浮出水面与产生。

entries.definition: The process of coming out or into existence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现、兴起」的过程。

entries.definition: Newly appearing or developing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「新兴的、刚出现的」。

entries.definition: To sink into or combine, from the same Latin verb without e-.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「合并、融入」，同一个拉丁动词去掉 e- 前缀。

entries.definition: To become visible, often without effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现」，常不带努力感。

entries.definition: To come up to the top, literally or figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浮出水面」，可实指也可比喻。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of problems or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「产生」，多用于问题或局面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read emerge as e- plus merge, out of the dip, then let the same rise become truth and new life.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 emerge 读成 e- 加 merge，即「从浸没中出来」，再让这次上升变成真相与新事物。

normal.en: E- means out and merge means sink, so emerge means rise out.
normal.cn: e- 表示向外，merge 表示下沉，所以 emerge 就是升出来。

normal.en: The sun emerges from the clouds.
normal.cn: 太阳从云层里露出来。

normal.en: Facts emerge when the water of secrecy drops.
normal.cn: 保密的水位一降，事实就露出来。

normal.en: A new market can emerge overnight.
normal.cn: 新市场可以在一夜之间兴起。

normal.en: A team can emerge stronger from a crisis.
normal.cn: 一个团队能从危机中变得更强。

abstract.en: Picture a dark shape rising slowly through water.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黑影从水下慢慢升起。

abstract.en: What was hidden becomes visible, and what did not exist begins to be.
abstract.cn: 藏着的东西变得可见，不存在的东西开始存在。

abstract.en: Emerge is a birth told as a surfacing.
abstract.cn: emerge 就是把诞生讲成一次浮出水面。

examples.en: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
examples.cn: 太阳从云层后露出。

examples.en: New facts emerged during the trial.
examples.cn: 审判过程中有新的情况显露出来。

examples.en: The small firm emerged stronger after the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机之后这家小公司变得更强。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一默己」——水下一声不响，忽然露头

root: 拉丁语 emergere，由 e-（向外）加 mergere（浸入、下沉）构成，字面为「从水中升起」。

sensesIntro.en: Emerge rises from water into sight, then into knowledge, then into existence, and finally out of danger.
sensesIntro.cn: emerge 先从水里升到视野中，再升到知识里，再升成新事物，最后升出危险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape rising through dark water until it breaks the surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团影子从暗水中升起，直到破开水面。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: the sun or a swimmer comes up.
branches.cn: 水面线：太阳或游泳者升出水面。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: hidden facts rise into view.
branches.cn: 真相线：隐藏的事实升入视野。

branches.en: THE NEW THING: an industry or trend begins.
branches.cn: 新事物线：产业或趋势开始出现。

branches.en: THE SURVIVOR: a person or firm comes out stronger.
branches.cn: 幸存线：人或公司更强地走出来。

branches.en: ONE RISE: water, truth and history share the same motion.
branches.cn: 同一次上升：水面、真相与历史共享同一个动作。

intro.en: Emerge is e-, out, plus the Latin root merg, sink, with the English verb ending -e.
intro.cn: emerge 是 e-（向外）加拉丁词根 merg（下沉），再接英语动词词尾 -e。

latinIntro.en: Mergere and emergere are both recorded Latin verbs of dipping and rising.
latinIntro.cn: mergere 与 emergere 都是有记录的拉丁语动词，分别表示浸入与升起。

definition_zh: 紧急情况；突发事件；急件
definition_en: a sudden dangerous situation that needs immediate action; used in such a situation
core_image: 平静的水面忽然炸开，所有人都得立刻行动
scene: 警报骤然响起，所有人朝安全通道跑去。The emergency exit was blocked by boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 emergency 是「紧急情况」（第 01 个义项：需要立即处理的危险局面）；句意是紧急出口被箱子堵住了。

pos.zh: 名词：紧急情况；突发事件
形容词（定语）：应急的；紧急的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ency 得到动词，义为「出现；浮现」
由 emerge 加 -ence 构成，义为「出现」
由 emerge 加 -ent 构成，义为「新兴的」

senses.title: A sudden dangerous situation
senses.definition: a sudden serious event that requires immediate attention
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生、需要立即处理的严重事件
senses.example: The emergency exit was blocked by boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急出口被箱子堵住了。
senses.why: The noun began as an unforeseen occurrence that suddenly rises up, so emergency is a situation that breaks through ordinary routine without warning.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词最早指突然「冒出来」的意外事件，所以 emergency 就是毫无预警地冲破日常秩序的处境。

senses.title: Used for such a situation
senses.definition: designed or kept for use in a sudden dangerous situation
senses.definitionCN: 为突发危险局面设计或保存的
senses.example: They kept an emergency fund for hard times.
senses.exampleCN: 他们存了一笔应急资金以备难关。
senses.why: A thing reserved for the sudden event borrows the event's name, so an exit, fund or room can all be called emergency.
senses.whyCN: 为突发状况预留的东西借用了状况的名字，所以出口、资金或房间都能用 emergency 作定语。

senses.title: An unforeseen occurrence, in older use
senses.definition: any unexpected event, an older and broader sense
senses.definitionCN: 任何未预料到的事件，是较旧且更宽的义项
senses.example: The diary records several emergencies of the voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 日记记下了航行中的几件意外。
senses.why: Before it specialised in danger, the word simply meant something that emerged unexpectedly, which is why old texts use it for any surprise.
senses.whyCN: 在专门表示危险之前，这个词只表示「意外冒出来的事」，所以旧文献里任何突发情况都能用它。

intro.en: Emergency is a noun built on emerge, and its earliest English sense was simply an unforeseen event.
intro.cn: emergency 是在 emerge 基础上构成的名词，英语中最早只表示「未预料到的事件」。

items.en: The verb meant to rise out or come up.
items.cn: 这个动词意为升起、浮现。

items.en: A late Latin noun named the act of coming up.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语名词表示「升起、出现」这一动作。

items.en: Emergency first meant an unforeseen occurrence.
items.cn: emergency 最初表示意外发生的事件。

items.en: The word narrowed toward sudden danger needing action.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，词义收窄为需要采取行动的突发危险。

items.en: The attributive use gave us emergency exit and emergency room.
items.cn: 定语用法又带来了 emergency exit 与 emergency room。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emerge family; the near-meaning group separates a crisis, a disaster and plain urgency.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emerge 词族展开；近义组区分危机、灾难与单纯的紧迫。

entries.definition: To come out or become known.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现、浮现」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: The process of appearing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现」的过程。

entries.definition: Newly arising.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「新兴的」。

entries.definition: A turning point of great danger or difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「危机」，强调转折点。

entries.definition: A sudden event causing great damage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灾难」，强调造成的巨大破坏。

entries.definition: The quality of needing immediate action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「紧迫性」，不一定是具体事件。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the sudden surfacing image, then let the noun name the event and the things kept ready for it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子保留「突然浮出」的画面，再让这个名词分别指事件与为它预备的东西。

normal.en: Emergency is what suddenly emerges.
normal.cn: emergency 就是突然冒出来的事。

normal.en: An emergency exit is a door kept for that moment.
normal.cn: emergency exit 就是为那一刻预留的门。

normal.en: A state of emergency suspends ordinary rules.
normal.cn: state of emergency 让日常规则暂停。

normal.en: Emergency services answer the sudden call.
normal.cn: 紧急救援部门回应突如其来的呼叫。

normal.en: The word began as any unforeseen event.
normal.cn: 这个词最早只是指任何意外事件。

abstract.en: Picture calm water breaking into a sudden splash.
abstract.cn: 想象平静的水面忽然炸开一朵水花。

abstract.en: The event and the equipment for it share one name.
abstract.cn: 事件与为事件准备的设备共用一个名字。

abstract.en: Emergency is routine interrupted without warning.
abstract.cn: emergency 就是毫无预警被打断的日常。

examples.en: The emergency exit was blocked by boxes.
examples.cn: 紧急出口被箱子堵住了。

examples.en: They kept an emergency fund for hard times.
examples.cn: 他们存了一笔应急资金以备难关。

examples.en: The diary records several emergencies of the voyage.
examples.cn: 日记记下了航行中的几件意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一默真稀」——平时不出声，一出就是稀罕大事

root: 由 emerge 加名词词尾 -ency 构成；emerge 出自拉丁语 emergere，字面为「从水中升起」，早期英语指意外发生之事。

sensesIntro.en: Emergency names a sudden dangerous event, the equipment kept for it, and in older use any unforeseen occurrence.
sensesIntro.cn: emergency 既指突发的危险事件，也指为它预备的设备，较旧时还泛指任何意外之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calm surface suddenly breaking into a splash.
core.cn: 核心意象：平静的表面忽然炸开一朵水花。

branches.en: THE EVENT: danger arrives without warning.
branches.cn: 事件线：危险毫无预警地到来。

branches.en: THE EQUIPMENT: exits, funds and rooms kept ready.
branches.cn: 设备线：出口、资金与房间随时待命。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: any unexpected occurrence.
branches.cn: 旧义线：任何未预料到的事情。

branches.en: EVENT AND PREPARATION: the name covers both.
branches.cn: 事件与预备：同一个名字两头都管。

branches.en: DANGER AND SURPRISE: danger is the narrowed form of surprise.
branches.cn: 危险与意外：危险义是意外义收窄后的结果。

intro.en: Emergency is emerge plus -ency, a noun ending that names a state or process.
intro.cn: emergency 是 emerge 加 -ency，这个词尾表示状态或过程。

latinIntro.en: The root mergere and the verb emergere are recorded Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 mergere 与动词 emergere 都是有记录的拉丁语形式。

definition_zh: 情感；情绪；感情
definition_en: a strong feeling such as love, anger or fear; a state of mental agitation
core_image: 心里有什么被搅动起来，一路涌到脸上
scene: 听到消息，她握着电话半天没说出话。Her voice shook with emotion.
sceneCN: 这里 emotion 是「情感、情绪」（第 01 个义项：强烈的内心感受）；句意是她的声音因情绪而发抖。

pos.zh: 名词：情感；情绪；感情

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「情感的；情绪化的」
由 emotional 加 -ly 构成，义为「情感上地」
由词干加 -ive 构成，义为「引起强烈情感的」

senses.title: A strong feeling
senses.definition: a strong feeling such as love, anger, fear or joy
senses.definitionCN: 爱、怒、惧、喜等强烈的内心感受
senses.example: Her voice shook with emotion.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音因情绪而发抖。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to move out, so an emotion is something stirred up inside and pushing outward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「向外移动」的动词，所以 emotion 就是心里被搅动起来、并向外推的东西。

senses.title: A particular feeling
senses.definition: one specific feeling, such as guilt, pride or grief
senses.definitionCN: 某一种具体的感受，如内疚、骄傲或悲伤
senses.example: He could not name the emotion he felt.
senses.exampleCN: 他说不出自己感受到的是哪种情绪。
senses.why: The general stirring can be divided into named kinds, so the same noun also counts individual feelings one by one.
senses.whyCN: 笼统的搅动可以分成分门别类的几种，于是同一个名词也用来逐一计数具体情绪。

senses.title: Mental agitation, in formal use
senses.definition: a disturbed or excited state of mind, often contrasted with calm reason
senses.definitionCN: 心绪受扰或兴奋的状态，常与冷静理性相对
senses.example: The speech appealed to emotion rather than reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演讲诉诸情感而非理性。
senses.why: When feelings are stirred strongly, they can override calm thought, so emotion also names agitation as a force opposed to reason.
senses.whyCN: 当感受被强烈搅动时，会压过冷静思考，所以 emotion 也指一股与理性相对抗的激动力量。

intro.en: Emotion entered English through French and ultimately goes back to a Latin verb meaning to move out.
intro.cn: emotion 经法语进入英语，最终可追溯到表示「向外移动」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Movere meant to move or stir.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、搅动。

items.en: With e-, out, the verb meant to move out or stir up.
items.cn: 加上 e-（向外）后，动词意为移出、激起。

items.en: Esmovoir and later emouvoir carried the sense of stirring feelings.
items.cn: esmovoir 及后来的 emouvoir 带有「搅动感情」的意思。

items.en: The noun named a stirring of the mind.
items.cn: 名词 émotion 指心绪被搅动。

items.en: English emotion settled on strong feeling and later on specific feelings.
items.cn: 英语 emotion 先固定为强烈感受，后又指具体情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emotion family; the near-meaning group separates feeling, sentiment and passion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emotion 词族展开；近义组区分感受、情感与激情。

entries.definition: Relating to or showing emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「情感的、情绪化的」。

entries.definition: In an emotional way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在情感上」。

entries.definition: Arousing strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引起强烈情感的」。

entries.definition: A general word for an inner sensation or attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感觉、感受」，是最宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: A view or feeling, often a refined or expressed one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「情感、观点」，常指较细腻或被表达出的感受。

entries.definition: A very strong emotion, especially love or anger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「激情」，强度高于一般 emotion。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read emotion as movement out of the mind, then let the stirring become a named feeling or a force against reason.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 emotion 读成「从心里往外移动」，再让这次搅动变成具体情绪或对抗理性的力量。

normal.en: E- out plus mov move: something stirred out.
normal.cn: e- 向外加 mov 移动：有东西被搅动着往外走。

normal.en: Strong emotion can shake a voice.
normal.cn: 强烈的情感能让声音发抖。

normal.en: Mixed emotions are several feelings at once.
normal.cn: mixed emotions 就是几种感受同时出现。

normal.en: Emotional is the adjective made with -al.
normal.cn: emotional 是加 -al 构成的形容词。

normal.en: An appeal to emotion opposes an appeal to reason.
normal.cn: 诉诸情感与诉诸理性相对。

abstract.en: Picture a still pond stirred by a hand from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一潭静水被水下的一只手搅动。

abstract.en: The word is movement first and a name for feelings second.
abstract.cn: 这个词先是「移动」，后来才成为感受的名字。

abstract.en: Emotion is weather inside a person.
abstract.cn: emotion 就是一个人内部的天气。

examples.en: Her voice shook with emotion.
examples.cn: 她的声音因情绪而发抖。

examples.en: He could not name the emotion he felt.
examples.cn: 他说不出自己感受到的是哪种情绪。

examples.en: The speech appealed to emotion rather than reason.
examples.cn: 那场演讲诉诸情感而非理性。
